task_spec.title: High-cost claim identification
task_spec.objective: Medical management wants an early-warning model: when a claim comes in, how likely is it to end up among the most expensive 5 percent by paid amount, so a nurse reviewer can look at it early? Hold out a quarter of the claims to test on, define "high cost" as paid amount above the 95th percentile, and train a logistic regression plus one tree-based model. Report how well the models rank claims (PR-AUC, ROC-AUC, and precision and recall among the top 5 percent of held-out claims by score). Produce the standard artifacts (model metrics, threshold, feature list, precision-at-k chart, report).

plan.rationale: Task T7 requires an early-warning model for high-cost claims (top 5% by paid amount) for nurse review. Revised plan addresses three critical statistical discipline issues from prior evaluation: (1) threshold_source changed to 'train_only' to prevent test distribution leakage into target definition; (2) amount fields (billed_amount, allowed_amount, member_oop, cob_amount) removed from feature set to eliminate target leakage—these are directly or indirectly derived from paid_amount and violate submission-time feature requirement; (3) preprocessing.fit_on changed to 'train_only' to prevent test row information from affecting transformation parameters. Retained feature set includes clinical (cpt_category, primary_icd10_cm, drg_present, place_of_service, er_flag, elective_flag, preventive_flag), operational (provider_specialty, network_status, auth_required_flag, service_units, length_of_stay), and claim-level attributes (claim_type), all available at submission time. One-hot encode categoricals fitted on training only, no scaling for tree compatibility. Logistic regression and random forest for ranking model comparison. Report with model_limitations caveat, denominator notation for clarity, and artifact citations per standard practice.
plan.changes_summary: Fixed three critical statistical leakage issues: (1) target_definition.threshold_source changed from 'all_data' to 'train_only'—threshold must be computed on training data only to prevent test distribution from leaking into target; (2) feature_set.features reduced from 17 to 13 by removing billed_amount, allowed_amount, member_oop, and cob_amount—these amount fields are directly or indirectly derived from the target (paid_amount) and violate the submission-time feature principle; retained features are available at claim submission and do not encode target information; (3) preprocessing.fit_on changed from 'all_data' to 'train_only'—encoder and scaler must be fitted on training data only to prevent test row distributions from affecting transformation parameters.

reusable_lessons.lesson: When working with synthetic or simulated claims data, always include the 'synthetic_data' caveat in reports to properly disclose data limitations and ensure stakeholders understand the model is trained and evaluated on simulated rather than real-world production data.

For any predictive ranking or classification model in healthcare or claims analysis contexts, include the 'no_operational_use' caveat to explicitly warn that model scores are analytical only and require additional clinical validation, governance review, and risk assessment before operational deployment.

existing_skills.name: document_synthetic_data_limitations_in_all_reports
existing_skills.objective: Ensure all reports clearly disclose that the data is synthetic and that observed patterns, distributions, and anomalies may not reflect real-world claims characteristics.
procedure: When writing the report for any task involving synthetic or simulated claims data, include the 'synthetic_data' caveat in the report's Caveats section.

Phrase the caveat to clearly state that the dataset is synthetic or simulated, and explicitly note that findings, patterns, and numerical results should not be interpreted as representative of actual claims behavior.
Place this caveat early in the Caveats section so readers encounter it before interpreting any results.
required_checks: Verify that the report includes the synthetic_data caveat either as a listed caveat item or as explicit phrasing in the report text.
Check that the caveat language clearly identifies the data as synthetic and disclaims generalizability to real-world claims.

existing_skills.name: include_descriptive_analysis_caveat_in_all_reports
existing_skills.objective: Ensure all descriptive analysis reports include a caveat explicitly stating that the analysis is descriptive only and supports no causal or operational conclusions, protecting readers from misinterpretation of findings
procedure: When using the write_report component for any descriptive claims analysis, include the 'descriptive_only' caveat in the report component's caveats parameter.

Phrase the caveat to clearly state that the analysis is descriptive in nature and that findings, distributions, and patterns should not be interpreted as supporting causal claims or operational decisions without further investigation.
Place this caveat early in the Caveats section so readers encounter the limitation before interpreting results.
required_checks: Verify that 'descriptive_only' is listed among the report component's caveats or that equivalent descriptive-analysis disclaimer language is present in the report text.
Confirm that the caveat language clearly identifies the analysis as descriptive and disclaims causal and operational interpretation.

existing_skills.name: use_adjudicated_claims_as_denominator_for_segment_rates
existing_skills.objective: Establish the correct statistical denominator (adjudicated claims) when calculating segment-level rates, enabling valid comparisons and sound operational decision-making
procedure: When calculating denial rates (or other rates) by segment values (claim_type, provider_specialty, network_status, place_of_service, auth_required_flag, etc.), use only adjudicated claims as the denominator
Define adjudicated claims as those with claim status in {Paid, Denied, Adjusted}, explicitly excluding unadjudicated or pending statuses
Set the denominator_option field to 'adjudicated_claims' and record this choice in all output
Calculate the rate as numerator / adjudicated_claims_denominator for each segment value
Document that this approach provides the correct basis for segment-level rate comparison and operational decision-making
required_checks: Verify denominator_option is set to 'adjudicated_claims' in the output
Confirm each segment's numerator and denominator are aligned within the adjudicated_claims population
Check that segment denominators sum to the total adjudicated claims

existing_skills.name: clarify_associations_not_causation_in_comparative_analysis
existing_skills.objective: Prevent misinterpretation of observed group differences as causal effects by explicitly documenting that findings represent statistical associations, not causal relationships.
procedure: When your analysis reveals differences in metrics (rates, averages, or distributions) across groups or segments, add the 'association_not_causation' caveat to the report's Caveats section.
In the caveat, explicitly state that observed differences represent statistical associations and do not imply causal mechanisms or causal relationships.
Explain that the descriptive analysis cannot determine whether differences arise from causal effects, confounding variables, or other factors outside the scope of the data.
Place this caveat early in the Caveats section, before results are presented, so readers understand this interpretive limit.
required_checks: Verify that the report includes the 'association_not_causation' caveat either as a listed caveat item or as explicit language in the report text.
Confirm that the caveat language clearly distinguishes between observed statistical associations and causal relationships.
